kurz: How, in spin-offs, takeovers and restructurings, an advantage arises from a seller being forced to sell, and less from better forecasts.

bloecke.md:
A special situation exists when a company's share is moved less by day-to-day business than by a legal or structural event with a date. Such events include a spin-off, a takeover offer, a capital measure or an insolvency plan. These cases share neither an industry nor a ratio. What connects them is the question of who has to act in this situation without regard to price, and who can wait.

Joel Greenblatt made this field well known. By his own account, his firm Gotham Capital achieved around 50% a year before and 30% after all fees from 1985 to 1994. At the beginning of 1995, he returned around $500 million to the outside partners. This shows that special situations can only absorb a limited amount of capital. They work in niches that are too small for large investors. Greenblatt's present-day Gotham Asset Management managed around $32.6 billion in March 2026 and has long worked with completely different, broadly diversified methods.

The discount in a special situation arises because someone has to sell, for example an index fund into which a share outside its index is booked, a mandate with a minimum market capitalisation, or a creditor who receives shares instead of money. What is rewarded is not having to sell yourself, regardless of how clever you are.

bloecke.unter: On the right, a date is fixed; at the top, the fair value is disputed; this determines whether a situation can be calculated or requires judgement.

felder.text: Neither a date nor a reliable value. The most difficult field and the only one in which a total loss can be the rule.
The spin-off date is fixed, but the fair value of the subsidiary is not. The initial discount results from selling pressure, regardless of the business.
Price and figures can be checked. All that is missing is the trigger that lifts the value. The purchases are a signal without a date.
Price and date are set out in the offer document. What is paid for is only the risk that the deal falls through.

bloecke.md:
## Initial discount in spin-offs

In a spin-off, a company transfers a business unit to a new company and books its shares into the securities accounts of its own shareholders. The shareholders have neither bought nor examined this position, and for many holders it does not fit their investment guidelines. Index funds that hold the parent company because of an index have to sell the subsidiary if it is not included in the same index. The same applies to funds with requirements on minimum size or region. The selling pressure of the first weeks therefore has nothing to do with the business that is being sold.

Three effects prolong the discount. First, there are initially no analyst estimates for the new company and no track record of its own against which it could be measured. Second, the remuneration of the new management board is usually aligned with the first share price, so a low starting level is in the interest of those who receive share options there. Third, before the spin-off, the parent alone decides how debt, pension liabilities and warranty provisions are allocated between the two companies.

The classic source for an excess return from spin-offs is the paper by Cusatis, Miles and Woolridge in the *Journal of Financial Economics* from 1993, on which Greenblatt also relies. It is over thirty years old, its data end before 1993, and the result figures are only accessible behind a paywall. Citations of the study as a promise of returns are therefore often based on figures that the person citing them has not read themselves. The mechanism described is reliable; the percentage figure is not.

The parent company usually also retains a stake. Daimler spun off Daimler Truck Holding with effect from 10 December 2021 and kept 35%, of which 5% went to the pension trust. Mercedes-Benz Group still holds around 30% today. Such residual stakes are regarded as an overhang because they will be sold at some point, and the market expects this.

bloecke.titel: The Siemens Energy spin-off in three phases
bloecke.unter: The same share shows that spin-offs start out undervalued and that they can nevertheless fail.

ereignisse.text: The first listing takes place on 28 September 2020 in Frankfurt. The shares are booked into the accounts of Siemens shareholders without them having bought or examined them. Siemens and its pension trust retain stakes.

After quality problems with onshore turbines, the share loses around 35% between 21 and 23 June 2023. In October 2023, the company negotiates with the Federal Government over guarantees, and the share price falls sharply again.
The share rises by more than 300% and reaches an all-time high. Investors who sold in 2023 because of the headlines added to the selling pressure that they themselves could have exploited.

bloecke.md: The structural initial discount says nothing about whether the spun-off business is economically viable. Often it is precisely the problem business that is spun off, and burdens that barely stood out in the consolidated financial statements then sit alone on a small balance sheet. The first stand-alone balance sheet and the spin-off report must therefore be examined in every case.

## Ownership thresholds in takeovers

In Germany, the takeover process is precisely regulated by law, and usable information can be gained from this. The ownership thresholds show what a major shareholder can do next and what they have to pay the minority for it. For assessing a takeover situation, voting rights notifications are therefore more informative than headlines. They can be used to work out which threshold can be reached next.

bloecke.titel: Ownership thresholds and their consequences (as of 2026)

bloecke.md:
The tax position in Germany is fairly simple, but it is often misjudged. Accepting a takeover offer counts as a sale. The gain is subject to the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% plus solidarity surcharge, together 26.375%, or around 27.8% to 28.0% with church tax. The same applies to the cash compensation in a squeeze-out. A subsequent top-up payment from appraisal proceedings is taxed in the year of receipt, which is often years later. The compensation payment from a domination agreement, on the other hand, is current capital income and is treated like a dividend.

The spin-off itself is an exception. Under Section 20(4a) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act), the new shares take the place of the old ones for tax purposes, the acquisition costs are split, and no taxable receipt arises. In the case of foreign spin-offs, however, German custodian banks often initially book the new shares as a taxable dividend in kind for lack of proof of comparability. A correction is possible, but it requires the transaction to correspond to a German spin-off. Investors who do not follow this up pay tax on a transaction in which they received nothing except a division of what already belonged to them.

## Merger arbitrage and deal-break risk

After a takeover offer, the target company's share trades below the offer price. This spread is a price for risks and not a market inefficiency. It compensates for the time until completion, for antitrust proceedings and conditions, and above all for the possibility that the deal fails. In that case, the share price falls back to the level before the offer. The calculation rests on the relationship between the spread as a possible gain and this price decline as a possible loss.

bloecke.titel: Illustrative calculation with an offer of €50.00, a price of €47.00, a pre-offer price of €38.00 and completion in 120 days

bloecke.md: The last row of the table shows the break-even point. With an upside of €3.00 and a downside of €9.00, the deal must go through with a probability of 75% for the expected result of the position to be zero. In general, the required probability of completion is obtained by dividing the possible loss by the sum of the possible gain and the possible loss. Without this calculation, you are merely buying a share with a very poor risk-reward ratio and not engaging in arbitrage.

bloecke.unter: The reference line shows the break-even probability from the illustrative calculation above; hostile offers are far below it.

bloecke.md: Merger arbitrage produces many small, predictable gains that in rare cases are lost again through large losses. This corresponds to the profile of an option writer who has sold a put option. Mitchell and Pulvino found an annualised return of 6.2% for 4,750 offers from 1963 to 1998. Baker and Savasoglu arrived at an excess return of 9.6% for 1,901 mergers from 1981 to 1996. These returns come at the price of a non-linear dependence on the overall market. If the overall market falls by 4% or more, the beta of the strategy rises to about 0.5, because deals fall through in greater numbers precisely when other investments are also falling. From 1990 to 2005, the HFRI Merger Arbitrage Index lost 6.5% in its worst month and gained only 2.9% in its best.

## Turnarounds and their financing

A turnaround, that is, the recovery of a company from a crisis, is a special situation without a date and without a forced seller. Unlike insider buying, it also lacks a reliable value. It therefore cannot be treated like the other three fields. Peter Lynch lists turnarounds as one of six categories of shares and requires a separate selling rule for them, because the expectation is fundamentally different. Here, the buyer is betting on insolvency being avoided, not on growth. There is no reliable, widely accepted success rate for turnarounds. Even the definition of success ranges from a restructuring that has been survived to a restored return on capital.

The financing, on the other hand, can be checked. More important than the question of whether the business is doing better again is the question of whether the maturities of the next two years are covered without existing shareholders being diluted through a capital increase. In a turnaround, it is almost always the creditors who benefit and rarely the shareholders. The order of priority in insolvency therefore determines who receives something in the end.

bloecke.quelle: Warren Buffett, Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter 1979

bloecke.md:
## Insider buying as a signal

Members of the management and supervisory boards and persons closely associated with them must report transactions in their own company's securities within three business days under Article 19 of the EU Market Abuse Regulation (MAR). The reporting obligation only applies once the total volume in the calendar year reaches €20,000. The national supervisory authority may raise this threshold to up to €50,000 or lower it to €10,000, and BaFin (Federal Financial Supervisory Authority) raised it to €50,000 for Germany with effect from 1 January 2026. In the thirty calendar days before an interim or annual report, these persons may not trade at all. The notifications are public and thus available to everyone. This raises the interesting question of whether they nevertheless have any information value.

The methodologically cleanest study on this comes from Jeng, Metrick and Zeckhauser. For reported insider transactions from 1975 to 1996, they formed rolling purchase and sale portfolios. The purchase portfolio achieved an excess return of around 40 basis points a month, the sale portfolio no measurable excess return. Around a sixth of the excess return accrued in the first five trading days, about a third in the first month. The study also contains two side findings. Small and large companies hardly differed, and members of the management board did not do better than other insiders.

bloecke.unter: An insider purchase is a voluntary decision, while there can be a hundred reasons for a sale, and this difference explains the finding.

bloecke.md:
1. The first thing to establish is who has to sell and for how much longer. Without an identifiable forced seller, there is no structural discount, only an opinion.
2. There has to be a date, such as a completion date, a general meeting or an entry in the commercial register. Without a date, the return per year is undetermined.
3. You need to check how far the price falls if nothing happens. Only this downside in relation to the upside gives the required probability of success.
4. The position size must match the deal-break risk. With losses that are rare but occur at the same time, large individual bets and leveraged implementations are unsuitable.

mitnehmen: The return in special situations comes from the forced selling of others, such as index funds, funds with mandate limits or creditors, and not from better forecasts.
In spin-offs, the mechanism is reliable, whereas the often-cited excess return figure from 1993 is not; what matters is the first stand-alone balance sheet and not the initial discount.
In Germany, the thresholds of 30, 75, 90 and 95% determine what a major shareholder may do next and what they have to pay the minority.
The required probability of completion of a merger arbitrage position is loss divided by gain plus loss; if the chance of completion is below this, the position is not arbitrage.
Insider purchases contain information, insider sales practically none, and turnarounds are the only field without a date and without a reliable value.

begriffe.text: Separation of a business unit into an independent company whose shares are booked into the securities accounts of the existing shareholders. In Germany, the transaction is tax-neutral under Section 20(4a) sentence 7 EStG, and the acquisition costs are split between parent and subsidiary.

Purchase of the share of a takeover target below the offer price after the takeover has been announced. The only thing rewarded is the risk that the deal fails and the share price falls back to the level before the offer.

Compulsory exclusion of the minority shareholders in return for cash compensation. It is possible from 95% of the share capital under Section 327a AktG, from 90% in the course of a merger under Section 62(5) UmwG and from 95% of the voting rights after an offer under Section 39a WpÜG.

Court proceedings under the Appraisal Proceedings Act (Spruchverfahrensgesetz) in which the adequacy of cash compensation or a compensation payment is reviewed. They regularly take several years, and a top-up payment is only taxed in the year of receipt.

Transactions by managers in their own company's securities that must be reported under Article 19 of the EU Market Abuse Regulation. From an annual volume of €20,000, in Germany from €50,000 since 2026, a reporting deadline of three business days applies, and in the 30 calendar days before an interim or annual report, trading is prohibited.
